9. STAFF DISCUSSION OF SIGNIFICANT ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS
The South Carolina State Highway Commission (SHC) has expressed concern regarding road and transmission line construction associated with the Bad Creek Project. The Applicant should cooperate and coordinate with SHC in the relocation of secondary system Road S-171 and in construction of transmission lines where State roads are crossed. SHC a o expressed concern on designating whose responsibility it would be to construct and maintain permanent and temporary access and construction roads.
As indicated in Table 1-1, Applicant would seek approval from SHC to relocate Highway S-171 in February 1977. Applicant should coordinate its roadbuilding activities with SHC and cooperate with reasonable requests made by this agency. Applicant would be expected to be responsible for relocating the 0.4-mile section of S-171 to SHC's specifications, and for construction and maintenance of access and construction roads within the project area. Applicant should also coordinate as necessary with SHC regarding construction of the permanent access road and tie-in with S-171. Applicant should coordinate road crossings of the proposed transmission line with SHC to minimize disruption of traffic-carrying functions on the roads crossed.
9.1 FLORA
Since rare or endangered plant species may be adversely affected by the proposed action, the Applicant should arrange for a preconstruction survey by a qualified botanist of all areas that may be disturbed and that have not been previously surveyed. This survey should include proposed spoil sites, borrow areas, roads, and other project facility sites. Should it be determined by the botanist that any number of rare or endangered plant species would be adversely affected by the proposed action, the Applicant should develop and implement an appropriate mitigation plan. Dr. C. Leland Rodgers has conducted a botanical survey of the proposed reservoir and transmission line right-of-way areas. The results of this survey relative to rare plant species are discussed in Section 2.2.3.1. Some measures that have been taken to mitigate expected adverse impacts to these rare plant forms are presented in Section 4.2.1.
